title.narrative: Public Space Regeneration Seminar: Exploring Sustainable Pathways for Urban Regeneration and Revitalization in Historic Centers of Megacities

description.narrative:
In the Third Phase of Global Public Space Programme (GPSP) (2020-2025), UN-Habitat has employed a strategic approach to public space encompassing a variety of normative and operational tools. These methodologies have been applied across diverse practices aiding local governments and other partners to make public spaces more safe, inclusive, accessible and green. Since 2013, GZPI has been involved in a series of collaborations with UN-Habitat in promoting sustainable urban development and improving living conditions. These collaborative efforts include talent exchanges, technical coopertion on some pilot planning projects in China and Africa, and joint compilation of report. Both UN-Habitat and GZPI are eager to strengthen and formalize this relationship into a long-term partnership by launching a six-month project aimed at delivering tangible outcome. In April 2024, UN-Habitat and GZPI have agreed to start a collaborative effort to advance the implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in cities globally and signed a MoU for further exploring potential joint practices in the following 5 years. Based on the previous partnership and framework outlined in the MoU, GZPI has proposed to contribute to the GPSP through organizing a seminar along with relevant technical discussions, bilateral meetings, and providing technical support to relevant projects in UN-Habitat HQ. This project will focus on supporting the dialogue around sustainable urban regeneration and the enhacement of public space, in particular in a context of historic districts in megacities. This collaboration aligns well with GPSP’s partner network building approach within the public space domain – strengthening the partnership with research institutions, which play an excellent role in capacity development, tool development, documentation, analysis, and monitoring.
The new collaboration will yield the following results:  Session/webinar/workshop organised for knowledge-sharing and mutrual learning among local authorities and professionals. The event will feature keynote speeches, topic presentations, panel discussions,and site visits, providing a platform for experts and city stakeholders to share insights and examples. It will highlight exemplary practices in sustainable urban regeneration.  Compile a publication based on the practices and inputs the experts share during and after the in-person seminar, with a focus on sustainable urban regeneration and revitalization in historic centers.  Maillist of internal and external experts for future network building with government departments, design institutes, universities, and professionals.
